posts.caption: Before work, I cut felt pads with the sharpened scissors. Clean edges at last. One chair has wandered off, so its pad is waiting.
posts.translationZh: 上班前用磨好的剪刀剪毛氈椅墊，邊緣終於俐落了。有張椅子不知道搬去哪裡，它的墊子只好先等著。
posts.imageAlt: Ada holding freshly cut felt chair pads in a breakfast alcove.
posts.storyContext: Ada puts her recently sharpened scissors to use before work, cutting felt pads for the breakfast chairs. The edges come out neatly, but one chair has been moved to another room, so she leaves its pad aside for later. She can discuss the difference sharpening made, keeping felt from shifting, and the small household jobs on her list.

posts.caption: My soup survived the walk to the courtyard. I put it down with both hands and immediately felt qualified to carry something much less important.
posts.translationZh: 湯平安抵達中庭了。我用雙手把它穩穩放下，瞬間覺得自己已經能搬運更不重要的東西。
posts.imageAlt: Bella setting an unmarked takeaway soup container on a courtyard table.
posts.storyContext: At Monday lunch, Bella carries a full container of hot soup out to the office courtyard. The lid shifts slightly, so she slows down and sets it on an empty table with both hands. She can talk about practical lunch choices, small kitchen mishaps, or why an ordinary walk briefly required so much concentration.

posts.caption: I spent my lunch break loosening a rope puzzle. It came apart while I was explaining why it couldn't. I may leave out the explanation next time.
posts.translationZh: 午休時研究了一個繩結機關，才剛解釋它為什麼不可能解開，它就散開了。下次也許省略解釋就好。
posts.imageAlt: Felix holding the loosened loops of a simple rope puzzle.
posts.storyContext: Felix brings a small rope puzzle to an unused office quiet room during Monday lunch. A loop slips free while he mentally argues that the configuration cannot work. He can discuss the step he overlooked, whether explaining a problem helps, or the difference between a useful theory and an entertaining wrong one.

posts.caption: Cold Monday mornings make my calves reluctant to start. A gentle stretch while waiting for the train helped. Mostly with the calves.
posts.translationZh: 冷冷的週一早上，小腿不太想開工。等車時輕輕拉一下有幫助，主要是對小腿有幫助。
posts.imageAlt: Finn gently stretching one calf on an empty commute platform.
posts.storyContext: Finn finds his calves stiff on a cold Monday morning. With time before his train, he stretches gently on a clear part of the platform, well back from the edge. The movement helps him warm up without rushing. He can discuss cold-weather warmups, his morning routine, or small exercises that fit into a commute.

posts.caption: I left the last spoonful of soup until I'd finished lunch. Apparently all the pepper waited there too.
posts.translationZh: 我把最後一口湯留到午餐吃完才喝。看來胡椒也一樣，全在那裡等我。
posts.imageAlt: Hugo sits with a nearly empty soup bowl at a quiet cafeteria table.
posts.storyContext: Hugo orders soup with Monday lunch and eats the solid ingredients before finishing the broth. A little pepper has settled at the bottom, making the final spoonful much stronger than expected. He decides that a quick stir would have helped. He can discuss soup habits, seasoning surprises, or the best part of a familiar lunch.

posts.caption: I started sketching a drip on the atrium glass at lunch. It changed direction twice. I feel this is unreasonable behaviour for a model.
posts.translationZh: 午休想畫中庭玻璃上的一滴水，它竟然改了兩次路線。我覺得模特兒這樣不太合理。
posts.imageAlt: Iris follows a condensation trail with a pencil sketch in a sheltered atrium.
posts.storyContext: Iris notices a droplet joining another condensation trail in a sheltered atrium during Monday lunch. Her pencil sketch stops matching the glass as the water changes course, and she keeps both paths on the page. She can discuss drawing moving subjects, unexpected patterns, or whether the extra lines improve the sketch.

posts.caption: One footnote has taken over my lunch break. It has a longer journey planned than the paragraph that sent me there.
posts.translationZh: 一則註腳占據了我的午休。它安排的旅程，似乎比帶我到這裡的正文還遠。
posts.imageAlt: Isla pauses over an open book on a quiet office breakroom chair.
posts.storyContext: Isla uses Monday lunch to read a few pages, but an unusually long footnote sends her away from the main argument. She marks her place with a finger rather than trying to finish before returning to work. She can discuss enjoyable digressions, footnotes that become stories, or whether she will remember the original paragraph later.

posts.caption: I shaped a scrap of foil into a moon while waiting for laundry after work. It keeps rolling away. Very independent orbit.
posts.translationZh: 下班等洗衣服時，我把一小片鋁箔捏成月亮。它一直滾走，公轉得非常有主見。
posts.imageAlt: Luna steadies a small foil ball on a home laundry shelf.
posts.storyContext: Luna waits for an evening laundry cycle and rolls a clean scrap of foil into a small moon for the shelf. The uneven ball will not stay where she puts it, so she experiments with a folded scrap as a base. She can discuss small things made while waiting, lunar shapes, or what sort of stand would keep the moon in place.

posts.caption: There's a gentler ramp on my Monday walk to work. It adds two minutes, but I can keep the same pace instead of stopping halfway up.
posts.translationZh: 週一走路上班，發現一條坡度比較緩的斜坡道。雖然多走兩分鐘，但可以維持步調，不用走到一半停下來。
posts.imageAlt: Max pauses beside a gently sloping public ramp on a cool Monday morning.
posts.storyContext: Max tests a public ramp as an alternative to the steep final stretch of his Monday commute. It takes slightly longer but feels better after a weekend of walking. He decides to use it when he is carrying a full bag. He can compare practical shortcuts, morning energy levels, or routes that are easier rather than faster.

posts.caption: Before work, an old lullaby caught me out. I knew the tune, but apparently I'd been inventing the second line for years.
posts.translationZh: 上班前，一首老搖籃曲讓我露餡了。旋律很熟，第二句歌詞居然是我自己編了好多年。
posts.imageAlt: Maya listens through earphones on an empty community porch in soft morning light.
posts.storyContext: Maya listens to an old lullaby recording through earphones before heading to work on Monday. The melody is familiar, but one line differs from the version she has always hummed. She pauses the recording to try her remembered version quietly. She can discuss songs learned by ear, half-remembered lyrics, or how familiar tunes change in memory.

posts.caption: I held the lift door for my shopping trolley. The little wheel still needed a personal invitation over the gap.
posts.translationZh: 我替買菜推車按住電梯門，那顆小輪子還是不肯過縫隙，得親手請它進來。
posts.imageAlt: Noah steadies his shopping trolley at the threshold of an empty lift lobby.
posts.storyContext: Before work on Monday, Noah brings his own shopping trolley downstairs to leave it in storage. One small wheel catches at the lift threshold, even with the door held open. He eases it over rather than pulling harder. He can talk about everyday awkward wheels, useful errands to combine, or the small amount of patience a normal morning needs.

posts.caption: I had a new key cut, and the basement door now requires a little persuasion. Same door, slightly more negotiation before work.
posts.translationZh: 我新打了一把鑰匙，地下室的門現在需要勸一下才肯開。同一扇門，上班前多了一點協商時間。
posts.imageAlt: Oscar pauses with a new key at a closed basement door on a Monday morning.
posts.storyContext: Oscar uses a newly cut key at the basement door before work on Monday. It fits but needs a gentle lift to turn smoothly, so he makes a note to have its edges checked rather than forcing it. He can discuss spare keys, small maintenance jobs, or the everyday objects that demand a surprisingly particular technique.

posts.caption: I made enough porridge for two mornings. The pot looked doubtful at first, but Monday breakfast is sorted.
posts.translationZh: 我煮了兩天份的粥。鍋子一開始看起來有點不太夠，不過星期一的早餐有著落了。
posts.imageAlt: Ryan turns from a kitchen hob beside a pot of porridge and two plain bowls.
posts.storyContext: Before work on Monday, Ryan cooks a little extra porridge so breakfast will be easier the next morning. The oats swell more than expected, making him keep a close watch on the pot. He can discuss sweet or savoury toppings, reheating leftovers and the small preparations that make his weekday mornings smoother.

posts.caption: I put a thin mat under my keyboard. The typing got quieter; my stomach chose that moment to be heard.
posts.translationZh: 我在鍵盤下面墊了一片薄墊。打字變小聲了，肚子偏偏選在這時候發出聲音。
posts.imageAlt: Theo slides a thin plain mat beneath a blank-key keyboard at an empty shared workspace.
posts.storyContext: On Monday morning, Theo checks whether a thin mat can reduce the keyboard noise at his shared workspace. The change is modest but noticeable in the empty room, until his stomach interrupts the comparison. He can discuss sound tests, breakfast timing and how much desk noise actually bothers him.

posts.caption: I tested my mended tote in the bicycle basket before work. The seam held; the loaf inside was the awkward part.
posts.translationZh: 上班前，我把補好的提袋放進腳踏車籃測試。縫線撐住了，反而是裡面的麵包不太好安頓。
posts.imageAlt: Yuna settles a mended tote containing a plain-wrapped loaf into a bicycle basket.
posts.storyContext: Yuna takes a tote repaired during an earlier home sewing session out for a practical Monday test. Its reinforced seam holds the weight, but a loaf makes the bag difficult to settle in the bicycle basket. She can discuss the repair, what she carries to work and the next adjustment she might make to the bag.

posts.caption: The bus arrived; my bench kept a shoelace. Apparently Monday thinks the furniture and I should leave together.
posts.translationZh: 公車到了，長椅卻扣住我的鞋帶。看來星期一覺得我應該帶著家具一起出發。
posts.imageAlt: Zoe frees a shoelace loop from a bench leg at an empty commuter shelter.
posts.storyContext: Before work on Monday, Zoe realises a loose shoelace loop has caught around the shelter bench leg as she starts to get up. She sits back briefly to free it and retie the shoe. She can discuss the minor delay, other improbable snags and what she was carrying that made the manoeuvre awkward.

posts.caption: My jacket zip caught its own lining. I freed it with a little patience, then zipped it once more because I needed to know we'd made peace.
posts.translationZh: 外套拉鍊夾住自己的內裡了。我慢慢把它解開，又拉了一次確認，總得知道我們和好了沒。
posts.imageAlt: Ada checking a freed jacket zipper beside a bedroom chair.
posts.storyContext: On Sunday afternoon, Ada frees a jacket lining caught in its zipper without pulling hard enough to tear it. She lays the jacket on a bedroom chair and checks the repaired section once more before putting it away. She can discuss zipper rescues, knowing when to stop tugging, or the clothing repairs she still wants to learn.

posts.caption: Two ends found, zero progress. I'm untangling decorative ribbon on a Sunday and neither end seems willing to help.
posts.translationZh: 找到兩頭，進度還是零。星期天在解布置用的緞帶，偏偏兩邊都不肯幫忙。
posts.imageAlt: Bella pausing over a tangle of plain ribbon on a dining bench.
posts.storyContext: Bella brings out a length of plain decorative ribbon for a small Sunday arrangement. It has knotted around itself in storage, so she spreads it across a dining bench and works out one loop at a time. She can discuss patient and impatient ways to untangle things, simple seasonal decorations, or the objects that never stay tidy in a drawer.

posts.caption: My pictureless jigsaw is finished. I moved it onto the spare-room floor to check the last gap. It was underneath my knee.
posts.translationZh: 沒有圖案的拼圖拼完了。我搬到客房地板上檢查最後一個缺口，結果那片就在我的膝蓋底下。
posts.imageAlt: Felix discovering the last piece beside a completed blank jigsaw.
posts.storyContext: Felix returns to the pictureless jigsaw from earlier in the week and moves it from the dining table to the spare-room floor for the final section. The last missing piece turns out to be under his knee. He can discuss the clues he used without a reference picture, protecting a nearly finished puzzle, and what makes a puzzle satisfying rather than annoying.

posts.caption: My rebound shot came back lower than expected. I caught it on the second bounce and decided that was the drill all along.
posts.translationZh: 回彈球比預期低，我等第二次彈起才接到，就決定這本來就是練習內容。
posts.imageAlt: Finn watching a tennis ball near an empty practice wall.
posts.storyContext: Finn spends a quiet part of Sunday hitting a tennis ball against an empty practice wall. One low return turns into a two-bounce catch rather than a clean shot. He can discuss adjusting to uneven rebounds, inventing small practice games, or how long he can keep a rally going on his own.

posts.caption: I made noodles for a quiet Sunday lunch. The thick ones and thin ones appear to have agreed on different cooking times.
posts.translationZh: 星期天安安靜靜做了碗手工麵。粗的跟細的，看來各自決定了不同的煮熟時間。
posts.imageAlt: Hugo stands beside a steaming pot with a tray of uneven handmade noodles.
posts.storyContext: Hugo spends Sunday making a small batch of noodles at home without a machine. The uneven widths become obvious once they reach the pot, and he begins adding the thicker pieces first. Lunch is later than planned but gives him something concrete to improve next time. He can discuss noodle thickness, cooking order, or the appeal of imperfect homemade food.

posts.caption: I gave a paper triangle a walk across my desk. Twelve photos later, it's travelled about as far as my Sunday plans.
posts.translationZh: 我讓紙三角形在桌上散步。拍了十二張之後，它走的距離跟我星期天的行程差不多遠。
posts.imageAlt: Iris arranges plain paper shapes beneath a phone stand on her home desk.
posts.storyContext: Iris uses plain paper scraps to try a short stop-motion scene at home on Sunday. Moving the triangle by tiny amounts takes more patience than she expected, and a slipped corner becomes part of its walk. She can discuss character through movement, small animation tricks, or whether the triangle needs another paper companion in a future scene.

posts.caption: I turned a thick page in the quiet archive and startled myself. My Sunday reading has unexpectedly acquired sound effects.
posts.translationZh: 在安靜的檔案室翻了一頁厚紙，結果被那個聲音嚇到。星期天的閱讀，突然多了音效。
posts.imageAlt: Isla browses a heavy volume in an empty archive reading nook.
posts.storyContext: Isla visits an archive reading nook on Sunday and notices how loudly the heavy paper turns in the still room. She slows down to lift one sheet cleanly, finding that the sound changes with her grip. She can discuss the physical feel of old books, quiet places, or whether paper changes the pace of reading.

posts.caption: I spotted mushrooms beside the trail that look like tiny umbrellas. I kept my hands to myself; their weather arrangements seem complete.
posts.translationZh: 步道旁的菇像一把把迷你雨傘。我沒伸手碰，它們的天氣安排看起來已經很完善了。
posts.imageAlt: Luna crouches beside small mushrooms on the edge of a woodland trail.
posts.storyContext: Luna walks a short woodland trail on Sunday and spots a small cluster of mushrooms beneath damp leaves. She crouches to look but leaves them untouched, imagining how much rain their caps might shelter. She can discuss miniature landscapes, careful nature watching, or the shapes she noticed on the rest of the walk.

posts.caption: My backpack cover kept the rain out until I found one damp corner. Apparently, I packed a tiny indoor weather system.
posts.translationZh: 背包防雨套擋住了雨，直到我摸到一個濕濕的角落。看來我還替背包準備了一套迷你室內天氣。
posts.imageAlt: Max checks one damp corner of a backpack cover on a quiet guesthouse balcony.
posts.storyContext: On Sunday, Max checks his backpack cover on the covered balcony of a small guesthouse. A light sprinkle reveals one damp seam, so he marks its position with a removable clip before packing up. The rest of the cover is dry. He can talk about checking outdoor gear, simple repairs, or the small discoveries that happen after a wet walk.

posts.caption: My balcony herbs finally made it into soup. I snipped one small sprig, then worried I'd given the whole pot a haircut.
posts.translationZh: 陽台上的香草終於加進湯裡了。我只剪了一小枝，就開始擔心是不是替整盆剪得太短。
posts.imageAlt: Maya snips a small sprig of homegrown herbs beside a steaming soup pot in her kitchen.
posts.storyContext: Maya brings a few leaves from her balcony herbs into Sunday's soup. The plants have grown slowly, so even one sprig feels like a noticeable harvest. She checks which stems to leave before putting the scissors away. She can talk about cooking with homegrown herbs, gentle pruning, or how much flavor a very small harvest can add.

posts.caption: My tea strainer slipped into the cup. I fished it out with a spoon, then let the tea cool while I cleaned the spoon. Fair enough.
posts.translationZh: 濾茶器滑進杯子裡了。我拿湯匙把它撈起來，再去洗湯匙，剛好順便讓茶涼一點。也好。
posts.imageAlt: Noah lifts a slipped tea strainer from a cup with a spoon on a sunroom bench.
posts.storyContext: During a slow Sunday afternoon in the sunroom, Noah loses his grip on the tea strainer and lets it drop into the cup. A spoon retrieves it without much drama. By the time he rinses the spoon, the tea is a comfortable temperature. He can talk about tea routines, peaceful afternoons, or minor mishaps that work themselves out.

posts.caption: I adjusted the deckchair to relax and ended up nearly horizontal. The sky was pleasant. Getting my tea was less convenient.
posts.translationZh: 我想把躺椅調舒服一點，結果差點整個躺平。天空是不錯，想拿茶就沒那麼方便了。
posts.imageAlt: Oscar checks the reclining position of a deckchair beside a cup on an empty roof terrace.
posts.storyContext: Oscar spends part of Sunday on an empty roof terrace and adjusts a deckchair one notch farther than intended. The low angle is comfortable until he wants the cup on the side table. He resets the chair before sitting again. He can discuss oddly designed furniture, relaxing in cool weather, or the practical limits of doing absolutely nothing.

posts.caption: I opened the bicycle bell to find its missing ring. The spring was fine; one tiny leaf had moved in.
posts.translationZh: 我拆開腳踏車鈴，想找回消失的鈴聲。彈簧沒壞，是一小片葉子搬進去了。
posts.imageAlt: Ryan stands beside an opened bicycle bell on a tray in an empty driveway.
posts.storyContext: Ryan spends a quiet Sunday afternoon checking a bicycle bell that has started sounding dull. He opens its cap over a tray and finds a tiny piece of leaf against the mechanism. He can talk about simple bicycle maintenance, the satisfying sound after cleaning it and the local rides he might take next.

posts.caption: I sorted mixed screws with an old colander. The smallest ones fell through; a washer stayed on top and somehow looked in charge.
posts.translationZh: 我拿舊濾盆分混在一起的螺絲。最小的掉下去了，一個墊圈留在上面，看起來莫名像在指揮。
posts.imageAlt: Theo stands at a shed workbench beside an old colander and sorted screws.
posts.storyContext: While tidying the shed on Sunday, Theo tests whether a coarse old colander can separate very small screws from a handful of larger parts. A wide tray catches the pieces that fit through the holes, while a large washer stays on top. The result is imperfect but entertaining. He can discuss improvised sorting tools, his next adjustment, or whether sorting by hand would have been quicker.

posts.caption: I threaded fallen seed pods on a piece of cotton. The smallest one keeps sliding into the middle, as if it booked the spot.
posts.translationZh: 我把掉落的種莢串上棉線。最小的那顆一直滑到中間，好像早就訂好位置了。
posts.imageAlt: Yuna threads dry fallen seed pods on cotton at a small patio table.
posts.storyContext: On a quiet Sunday afternoon, Yuna gathers a few dry seed pods blown onto her patio and threads them through their natural openings. One tiny pod slides to the low point whenever she lifts the cotton. She can discuss autumn finds, whether the little decoration will hang straight and other objects she likes to keep briefly.

posts.caption: I hooked a tiny plush at the fair. It's barely bigger than my thumb, but I'm carrying it like a major sporting trophy.
posts.translationZh: 我在市集用小鉤子釣到一隻迷你絨毛玩具。它只比拇指大一點，我卻拿得像剛贏了什麼大賽。
posts.imageAlt: Zoe lifts a tiny plain plush with a hook at an empty outdoor fair game booth.
posts.storyContext: Zoe stops at a small fair game on Sunday and carefully hooks a tiny unbranded plush from a shallow tray. The prize is comically small compared with the attention she gives it. She can talk about games that require patience, the creature she thinks it resembles and where the miniature prize will end up.

posts.caption: Saturday's drawer dividers are done. My screwdriver fits beautifully. The drawer won't close until I move the spare screws.
posts.translationZh: 星期六的抽屜隔板做好了，螺絲起子放進去剛剛好。不過得先移走備用螺絲，抽屜才關得起來。
posts.imageAlt: Ada fitting cardboard dividers into an open drawer in a small craft shed.
posts.storyContext: Ada spends part of Saturday sorting a tool drawer in a small craft shed. Her cardboard dividers fit, but a forgotten heap of spare screws blocks the drawer. She shifts the screws into a shallow dish instead of rebuilding everything. She can discuss tool storage, measuring mistakes, and which objects deserve a compartment of their own.

posts.caption: One very soft persimmon has changed my market plans. It needs a spoon, so eating while walking lasted about six seconds.
posts.translationZh: 一顆熟透的柿子改變了我的逛市集計畫。它得用湯匙吃，邊走邊吃的打算大概只維持了六秒。
posts.imageAlt: Bella scooping a soft persimmon beside an unattended fruit stall.
posts.storyContext: Bella picks a soft persimmon during a Saturday market visit and discovers that walking with it is a poor plan. She stops at an empty stall-side perch with a small spoon and takes her time. She can discuss choosing ripe fruit, food that is harder to eat than expected, or what caught her attention elsewhere in the market.

posts.caption: I picked the flattest stone by the pond. One skip. I clearly spent too much time interviewing candidates and not enough practising.
posts.translationZh: 我在池邊挑了最扁的石頭，結果只彈了一下。顯然挑選候選人的時間太長，練習的時間太少。
posts.imageAlt: Felix selecting a flat stone on a quiet pond bank.
posts.storyContext: On Saturday, Felix stops by a quiet pond and spends longer selecting a flat stone than throwing it. His best attempt makes one skip before sinking. He can discuss the angle of a throw, whether stone shape or practice mattered more, and the pleasure of a small experiment with no score to keep.

posts.caption: That short hill looked much shorter before my Saturday sprints. The walk down is now my favourite section.
posts.translationZh: 那個短坡在我週六衝刺之前，看起來明明比較短。現在走下坡成了我最喜歡的部分。
posts.imageAlt: Finn recovering beside a grassy incline after a short uphill sprint.
posts.storyContext: Finn chooses a grassy incline for a few short Saturday sprints. The slope feels steeper in motion than it looked from below, so he gives himself a full walk down between attempts. He can discuss pacing, choosing a hill, or the gap between planning an exercise session and actually starting it.

posts.caption: I picked the biggest rice dumpling at the market. Halfway through, I'm respecting how much chewing one little parcel can require.
posts.translationZh: 我在市集挑了最大顆的粽子。吃到一半，我開始尊敬這小小一包需要的咀嚼功力。
posts.imageAlt: Hugo examines an opened rice dumpling at an otherwise empty market counter.
posts.storyContext: Hugo stops at a market counter during a cool Saturday outing and chooses a rice dumpling wrapped in leaves. Its chewy texture makes the small snack take longer than expected, so he settles in rather than eating while walking. He can discuss different dumpling textures, patient snacking, or how a market visit became a long lunch.

posts.caption: Today's leaf rubbing looks like a tiny road map. I've found several routes on it that go absolutely nowhere.
posts.translationZh: 今天拓的落葉像張迷你路線圖。我在上面找到好幾條路，走到最後都沒地方可去。
posts.imageAlt: Iris makes a leaf rubbing at an empty garden pavilion table.
posts.storyContext: Iris collects one dry fallen leaf during a Saturday walk and makes a rubbing under a garden pavilion. Its broken veins create a surprisingly map-like pattern, with gaps she did not notice on the leaf. She keeps the imperfect version instead of starting again. She can discuss found textures, imaginary places, or how much detail a simple rubbing captures.

posts.caption: Two copies of the same unread essay turned up on my shelf. Apparently I've been meaning to read it with unusual commitment.
posts.translationZh: 書架上翻出兩份還沒讀的同一篇散文。看來我對「改天要讀」這件事，有異常堅定的決心。
posts.imageAlt: Isla sorts two plain essay booklets beside a hallway shelf at home.
posts.storyContext: Isla spends part of Saturday clearing a hallway shelf and discovers two copies of an essay she has yet to read. She puts one in a separate pile to pass on, keeping the other within easy reach. She can discuss duplicate books, the reading pile she actually uses, or what makes an unread piece linger for months.

posts.caption: I slept late and found a crescent-shaped dent in my pillow. Apparently I had a moon appointment and managed to sleep through it.
posts.translationZh: 睡到很晚，發現枕頭上壓了一道月牙。看來我跟月亮有約，卻一路睡過去了。
posts.imageAlt: Luna inspects a crescent-shaped crease in a pillow on a rumpled bed.
posts.storyContext: Luna wakes late on Saturday and notices a curved crease in the pillow after sitting up. She straightens the sheet but leaves the pillow for a moment because the shape looks so deliberate. She can discuss slow weekend mornings, odd sleep marks, or whether breakfast is still breakfast near noon.

posts.caption: I finished the walk, but my boots brought half the trail with them. A little wooden peg has become essential equipment.
posts.translationZh: 步道走完了，鞋底卻順便帶回半條路。現在這根小木釘，已經升格成必備裝備。
posts.imageAlt: Max clears mud from a boot sole with a wooden peg at a country trailhead.
posts.storyContext: Max ends a cool Saturday walk at a muddy country trailhead. Before getting back into the car, he notices how much clay is packed into the grooves of his boots. A small wooden peg clears the stubborn bits without damaging the soles. He can discuss muddy routes, what he keeps in his walking bag, or the less glamorous end of an outdoor day.

posts.caption: I chose the squash that wouldn't sit flat. It needed a folded towel for the ride home, which feels like special treatment.
posts.translationZh: 我挑了一顆怎麼放都放不穩的南瓜。載它回家還得墊條摺好的毛巾，這待遇好像有點太好了。
posts.imageAlt: Maya steadies an uneven squash on a plain wooden crate inside a farm shed.
posts.storyContext: On Saturday, Maya buys an unusually shaped squash from a small farm shed. Its rounded base keeps rolling on the crate, so she plans to cushion it with a folded towel on the way home. She is more interested in how it will cook than how tidy it looks. She can discuss market finds, squash recipes, or the awkward things people manage to carry home.

posts.caption: The stool no longer catches my sleeve. I only sanded one rough edge, then sat there longer than the job had taken.
posts.translationZh: 木凳終於不會勾住我的袖子了。我只磨平一小塊粗邊，後來坐著的時間反而比做事還久。
posts.imageAlt: Noah smooths the edge of a wooden stool with sandpaper in an empty courtyard.
posts.storyContext: On Saturday, Noah notices that the edge of an old wooden stool keeps catching his sleeve. He brings a small piece of sandpaper into the courtyard and smooths only the rough patch. Testing it turns into a longer sit in the cool sunshine. He can talk about small household repairs, comfortable corners, or things that become nicer through a little attention.

posts.caption: My small parcel arrived with six pieces and one spare screw. I have decided it is spare. The assembly seems to agree so far.
posts.translationZh: 小包裹到了，裡面有六個零件，最後多出一顆螺絲。我決定當它是備用的。目前組好的東西也沒反對。
posts.imageAlt: Oscar checks an assembled plain coat hook beside a small open parcel on a hallway console.
posts.storyContext: On Saturday, Oscar assembles a small freestanding coat hook from a parcel on his hallway console. One screw remains after all the joints are secure, so he tests the stand gently and keeps the screw in a small dish. He can discuss flat-pack mysteries, how to identify spare parts, or the modest satisfaction of a useful new household object.

posts.caption: I cleared the leaves from the garden drain. A surprising amount of Saturday was hiding under one wet leaf.
posts.translationZh: 我把花園排水孔的落葉掃開。沒想到一片濕葉子底下，藏著這麼多星期六的工作。
posts.imageAlt: Ryan brushes wet fallen leaves away from a small garden drain.
posts.storyContext: On Saturday morning, Ryan notices a shallow puddle collecting beside the garden drain. Clearing the visible leaf reveals a much thicker layer underneath. The job takes longer than expected, but the water begins moving again. He can discuss autumn garden chores, useful outdoor tools and how he divides up a slow weekend.

posts.caption: I bounced a torch off a plain card in the attic. Softer light, fewer dramatic shadows on the laundry basket.
posts.translationZh: 我在閣樓用一張白卡反射手電筒的光。光線柔和多了，洗衣籃也沒那麼像驚悚片道具了。
posts.imageAlt: Theo adjusts a plain white card to soften a torch beam in an attic.
posts.storyContext: Theo uses a quiet Saturday to sort an attic corner. A harsh torch beam makes every basket cast an enormous shadow, so he experiments with bouncing the light off plain white card. He can discuss simple lighting experiments, finding forgotten household objects and how little equipment a useful test can require.

posts.caption: In the stall's shade, my two fabric scraps matched perfectly. In daylight, they immediately had different opinions.
posts.translationZh: 攤位陰影裡，我挑的兩塊零布明明很搭。拿到日光下，它們馬上各有意見了。
posts.imageAlt: Yuna holds two plain fabric remnants at an empty outdoor fabric stall.
posts.storyContext: Yuna browses leftover fabric at a weekend market and compares two small pieces she thought would go together. Moving them from the awning shade into daylight changes the match. She can discuss colour surprises, possible small sewing projects and whether she kept the unexpected pairing.

posts.caption: I put a spoon in my apron pocket while baking. It slid out when I bent down, so apparently the pocket has limits.
posts.translationZh: 烤東西時，我把湯匙塞進圍裙口袋。一彎腰它就滑出來了，原來這口袋也是有能力範圍的。
posts.imageAlt: Zoe picks up a spoon beside her oven while wearing a plain baking apron.
posts.storyContext: During Saturday baking, Zoe uses her apron pocket as temporary storage for a spoon. Bending to check the oven sends it sliding onto the floor, giving her one more thing to wash. She can discuss her current baking attempt, surprisingly unhelpful pockets and which utensil she keeps misplacing.

posts.caption: My lunch table kept rocking. One folded bit of card fixed it, and now I'm reluctant to move my elbow and upset the engineering.
posts.translationZh: 午餐的桌子一直晃，一小片摺好的厚紙就解決了。現在反而不敢移開手肘，怕破壞這項工程。
posts.imageAlt: Ada sliding a folded card beneath a rocking cafe table leg.
posts.storyContext: During lunch, Ada notices that her table rocks whenever she reaches for her plate. A clean scrap of thick card becomes a temporary shim. She checks that it stays clear of the walkway and plans to mention the uneven leg before leaving. She can talk about improvised fixes, choosing a shim thickness, or the little problems she notices while eating.

posts.caption: I booked a little singing booth after work and forgot half the words. My humming was extremely committed, though.
posts.translationZh: 下班後租了小小的練唱包廂，結果一半歌詞都忘了。不過哼旋律的部分，我可是非常投入。
posts.imageAlt: Bella humming into a microphone in an empty practice booth.
posts.storyContext: Bella spends a short Friday evening in a solo singing booth. With the display switched off, she discovers how much of a familiar song she only knows as a tune. She enjoys humming through the gaps rather than restarting. She can discuss songs remembered imperfectly, choosing a comfortable key, or whether humming counts as knowing the chorus.
